Second life for electric car batteries. This is the idea from Team Five, Battery Monster.
An electric car battery leaves the car when it has lost about twenty to thirty percent of its capacity. It is too weak for driving, but far from dead.
The problem? In Latvia there is no clear place to take these batteries. Only a few retire each year, nobody tests them properly, and nobody takes responsibility for safety and recycling.
Our idea is a take-back and testing hub. Fleets, car dismantlers and insurers bring us used batteries, and we check every one of them.

After testing, each battery goes one of three ways. The best ones, about thirty percent in our plan, are sold to Engy cell for a second life as storage. Some we take apart in Latvia. The rest go to a specialist recycler in Poland.
Most batteries, about seventy percent in our plan, are recycled. We shred them, and sell copper, aluminium, steel and black mass, the powder that holds nickel, cobalt and lithium, to refiners.
The good batteries get a second life. Small storage units next to electric chargers and bus depots, where the grid is weak, store power when it is cheap, and release it when it is needed.
So there is one responsible partner for safety, paperwork and recycling. Less waste, more reuse, and a circular economy for Latvia.
We start small, with a pilot. Team Five, Battery Monster.
